content:
Here's the translation in English:

Then in turn addressed him the lord of men, Agamemnon:
'I rejoice, son of Laertes, hearing your speech.
For you have gone through everything in due order and narrated it well.
And I wish to swear this, and my heart bids me,
And I shall not commit perjury against the divine. But let Achilles
Remain here, though he is eager for battle.
Let all the others remain gathered, until the gifts
Come from the tent and we cut trustworthy oaths.
And to you specifically, I now give this instruction and command:
Select the best young men from all the Achaeans
And bring the gifts from my ship, as many as we promised to give Achilles yesterday,
And bring the women.
And let Talthybius quickly prepare a boar throughout the wide army
To sacrifice to Zeus and to the Sun.'

This appears to be a passage from Homer's Iliad, specifically from a scene involving Agamemnon discussing oaths and gifts with Odysseus (the son of Laertes).
